9 Best Software Development Agencies for Enterprise Teams (2026)

"Software development agency" covers wildly different businesses under one search term. It can mean a 2,000-engineer outsourcing firm in Eastern Europe, a 20-person AI-native shop that ships a working product in 30 days, or a curated marketplace that matches you with a single freelance engineer. Picking the wrong shape for your actual problem costs months, not just budget.

Disclosure: ManasFlow publishes this list and ranks itself first. Every other agency was scored on the same rubric below, and every Clutch figure cited for every agency, including ours, was pulled live on September 5, 2026 (N-iX added September 8, 2026, same live-pull standard). Where a number couldn't be independently confirmed, this guide says so instead of guessing.
What enterprise software development agencies deliver

Enterprise software development is the design, build, integration, and long-term support of custom software for large organizations, under their security, compliance, and procurement rules. Agencies sell it in one of three shapes: a dedicated team billed by the month (BairesDev, AgileEngine), a scoped project with a fixed deliverable (ManasFlow, Fingent), or a marketplace that matches you with individual engineers (Toptal). Product design and development agencies such as Netguru add UX research and interface design to the same build. Pick the shape first, then the firm.

How we ranked these agencies

Four criteria, applied the same way to every entry: (1) Delivery model clarity: does the agency state plainly whether you get a dedicated team, a project-based build, or a marketplace match, or does that only surface after a sales call? (2) Verified reputation: real, checkable Clutch reviews rather than a testimonials page an agency controls itself. (3) Pricing transparency: published hourly rates and minimum project sizes, not "contact us for a custom quote" with nothing else. (4) Specialization depth: does the agency have a real, checkable edge (an industry, a technology, a delivery speed), or is it a generalist that competes purely on headcount?

1. ManasFlow, best for AI-native full-service builds and embedded engineers

ManasFlow pairs one senior engineer with a fleet of AI agents to cover what a traditional team of several developers would deliver, across strategy, build, QA, and maintenance. Its SaaS MVP development service ships a live product in a fixed 30-day sprint, and its custom automation work builds n8n workflows and AI agents that run around the clock, not a one-time script. For enterprise teams that need software built around their own data and systems, our custom AI development company page covers scope and process.

Why we rank ManasFlow #1: not on adjectives, on checkable evidence. An engineer-placement model most agencies on this list do not offer: a 2 to 4 week placement window and a 90-day replacement guarantee for teams that need embedded capacity rather than a single fixed-scope project (see hire AI developers). A fixed 30-day MVP delivery window most agencies won't commit to in writing. Multilingual delivery (English, French, Arabic).

What we will not claim: broad press coverage or a large public review count. ManasFlow's Clutch profile carries 3 verified reviews at 5.0/5 as of September 2026, the smallest review count on this list, disclosed here with the same evidence bar every other agency is held to.
Best for: teams that want a single partner for strategy through maintenance, and teams that need embedded engineering capacity (not just a project) filled in weeks, not months.
Pricing: custom project-based pricing; fractional CAIO retainer available for ongoing AI strategy; staff augmentation with 2-4 week placement and a 90-day replacement guarantee.
Pros: single partner covers the full lifecycle; 30-day MVP model is a written commitment, not a best-effort estimate; embedded placement option most competitors on this list don't offer.
Cons: the smallest public review count on this list; no self-serve platform for teams that want to build with their own tooling.
2. BairesDev, best for large-scale nearshore staff augmentation

BairesDev is a Latin American nearshore staffing and development firm built for enterprises that need to add engineering capacity at scale, fast. Its Clutch profile shows a 4.9/5 rating across 63 verified reviews, with reviewers most often citing responsiveness and developer quality.
Best for: enterprises that need to scale an internal team with nearshore engineers across a wide range of stacks, rather than hand off an entire project to an outside partner.
Pricing: $50-99/hr, $50,000+ minimum project size; published project ranges from $10,000 to over $5 million depending on scope.
Pros: large bench of engineers across many technologies and time zones aligned to US business hours; strong Clutch review volume.
Cons: staff-augmentation model still requires internal management capacity; pricing sits at the higher end of the nearshore agencies on this list.
3. Netguru, best for digital product design paired with fintech engineering
Netguru is a Polish digital product consultancy with 800+ professionals, known for strong design capability alongside engineering, particularly in fintech. Clutch shows 71 verified reviews at 4.8/5.
Best for: teams where product design quality is as important as the engineering, especially in regulated fintech contexts.
Pricing: $50-99/hr, $50,000+ minimum project size; publicly cited project costs range from under $5,000 to over $500,000 depending on scope.
Pros: design and engineering under one roof avoids handoff friction between two separate vendors; strong fintech-specific track record.
Cons: minimum project size and rate sit above the accessible end of this list; better fit for larger, design-heavy engagements than a small fixed-scope build.
4. AgileEngine, best for dedicated teams at an accessible rate

AgileEngine is a US-headquartered software engineering partner, founded in 2010, with distributed teams across the US, Poland, Ukraine, Colombia, Argentina, Brazil, India, and Mexico. Clutch shows a 5.0/5 rating across 63 verified reviews, the highest rating of any agency on this list.
Best for: enterprises and venture-backed startups that want a dedicated team model without the higher rates of the larger nearshore firms above.
Pricing: $25-49/hr, $25,000+ minimum project size; published projects range from $15,000 to over $450,000.
Pros: perfect 5.0/5 rating across a real review count; lower rate band than BairesDev or Netguru for a comparable dedicated-team model.
Cons: broader generalist positioning than the AI/ML- or fintech-specific agencies on this list.
5. Simform, best for AI/ML-forward product engineering

Simform is a digital engineering company with 500+ engineers, an AWS Advanced Partner, placed in Clutch's Market Leaders quadrant for both AI development and machine learning. Clutch shows 86 verified reviews at 4.8/5, the largest review count on this list.
Best for: teams whose build leans specifically on AI/ML, cloud, or data engineering rather than general full-stack work.
Pricing: $25-49/hr, $25,000+ minimum project size; pricing set through a structured discovery and estimation phase rather than a flat rate card.
Pros: largest independently verified review count on this list; specific Clutch recognition in AI and ML, not just general software development.
Cons: co-engineering model requires real client-side involvement in the discovery phase before pricing is finalized.
6. Fingent, best for long-track-record enterprise custom software
Fingent has been delivering custom software since 2003, with more than 700 completed projects for clients including Mastercard, Sony, and PwC. Clutch shows 66 verified reviews at 4.9/5.
Best for: enterprises that weight a two-decade delivery history and named enterprise clients heavily in vendor selection.
Pricing: $25-49/hr, $25,000+ minimum project size; published project costs range from $12,500 to over $2 million.
Pros: longest operating history of any agency on this list; named enterprise client roster is independently checkable, not just claimed.
Cons: a longer operating history does not by itself guarantee the fastest delivery timeline; confirm current team availability and timeline before assuming legacy scale translates to speed.
7. ELEKS, best for large-scale full-cycle enterprise engineering
ELEKS is a full-cycle software development and technology consulting firm founded in 1991, with more than 2,000 specialists across 17 offices. Clutch shows 31 verified reviews at 4.8/5.
Best for: enterprises that need full-cycle delivery, including product design and technology advisory, at a scale most boutique agencies on this list cannot match headcount-for-headcount.
Pricing: $50-99/hr, $25,000+ minimum project size; the most common cited project range on Clutch is $200,000-$999,999.
Pros: three-decade operating history and large specialist headcount support genuinely large, multi-year engagements.
Cons: smallest verified review count relative to headcount on this list; typical project sizes skew toward large enterprise budgets rather than smaller builds.
8. Toptal, best if you want one freelance engineer, not an agency team

Toptal is not an agency. It's a curated marketplace: you submit a hiring need, a client advisor matches you with vetted freelance engineers from what Toptal describes as the top 3% of applicants, and you manage the engineer directly rather than working with an agency delivery team.
Best for: a single specialized hire or a small curated team, not a full project handoff, and teams that want to start in days rather than weeks.

Pricing: a $79/month subscription fee, a $500 refundable deposit, and hourly rates typically between $60 and $150+/hr depending on specialization; Toptal applies an additional markup on top of what the engineer is paid that is not disclosed to the client.
Pros: fast matching, typically 5-7 days to a hire; a trial period where you pay only if satisfied before committing further.

Cons: it is a talent marketplace, not a delivery partner. You still own project management, architecture decisions, and QA yourself. No agency-style accountability for outcomes the way the other 7 entries on this list provide.

9. N-iX, best for named enterprise clients and analyst recognition

N-iX is an engineering firm founded in Ukraine in 2002, now with a global office network spanning Malta, Poland, the US, UK, Sweden, Colombia, Ukraine, Bulgaria, Romania, and India, and 2,400+ engineers. Its homepage lists Bosch, Siemens, Lebara, eBay, Inditex, AutoScout24, Credit Agricole, and TotalEnergies among its clients, confirmed directly on n-ix.com rather than taken from a third-party summary — several of these are large multinational enterprises, not US Fortune 500 companies specifically. Clutch shows 35 verified reviews at 4.8/5, and its own profile page lists recognition from Forrester, Everest Group, DataIQ, CRN Solution Provider 500, IAOP's Global Outsourcing 100, and ISG Provider Lens, plus AWS and Snowflake Premier Tier Partner status — these come from N-iX's Clutch listing and weren't independently cross-checked against each analyst firm's own site.
Best for: enterprises that weight named, checkable large-enterprise client relationships and third-party analyst recognition (per its Clutch listing) over review count alone.
Pricing: $50-99/hr, $100,000+ minimum project size, the highest minimum on this list, well above the $50,000+ tier of BairesDev and Netguru.

Pros: client list is independently verifiable on the company's own site, not just a Clutch claim; multiple named analyst-firm recognitions (Forrester, Everest, ISG) most agencies on this list don't have; AWS and Snowflake partner tiers signal real cloud-delivery depth.
Cons: $100,000+ minimum prices out smaller projects entirely; fewer verified Clutch reviews (35) than Simform, Netguru, Fingent, or BairesDev, despite a larger headcount than most of them.
Red flags when evaluating a software development agency
None of these disqualify an agency by themselves, but each has cost a client real time or money in cases we've seen.
A fixed-price quote with no one named as responsible for the codebase after handoff. Something has to own the software when it breaks. If no one is named in the contract, it's you by default.
A portfolio of logos with no case study detail: no named metric, no before/after number, no description of what was actually built.
Vague pricing that only appears after a discovery call, with no ballpark offered up front, not even a wide one.
A dedicated-team pitch that turns out to be a revolving set of contractors with no continuity between sprints.
No willingness to show a sample of actual code or a past client's working product, even redacted.
A sales contact who can't describe how the team handles code review, testing, or handoff documentation without looping in someone else.
How to choose the right software development agency
1) Do you need a team, a project, or a single hire?

Dedicated-team agencies (AgileEngine, BairesDev, Netguru) embed engineers into your existing process. Project-based agencies (ManasFlow, Fingent, ELEKS, Simform) own a defined scope from start to finish. A marketplace (Toptal) hands you one engineer and leaves the project management to you.
2) How specialized is the build?
A generalist full-stack build fits most agencies on this list. An AI/ML-heavy build favors Simform or ManasFlow specifically. A design-critical fintech product favors Netguru.
3) What's your budget and minimum viable engagement size?

AgileEngine, Simform, and Fingent start around $25,000. BairesDev and Netguru start around $50,000. N-iX starts at $100,000+, the highest minimum on this list. ManasFlow and Toptal don't publish a fixed minimum; ManasFlow scopes to the project, Toptal scopes to the individual hire.
4) Do you need ongoing maintenance or a one-time build?

If the software is business-critical, ask specifically who owns it after handoff. ManasFlow includes 24/7 automation maintenance as part of its embedded model; several of the larger firms on this list price maintenance as a separate retainer, so confirm before you sign.
Which agency fits your case
Choose ManasFlow if you want one partner from strategy through maintenance and a written 30-day delivery commitment for an MVP.
Choose BairesDev if your bottleneck is headcount at enterprise scale, not strategy.
Choose Netguru if design quality and fintech depth matter as much as raw engineering throughput.
Choose AgileEngine if you want a dedicated team model at a lower rate than the largest nearshore firms.
Choose Simform if your build is genuinely AI/ML-heavy rather than general full-stack work.
Choose Fingent or ELEKS if you weight decades of operating history and named enterprise clients heavily.
Choose Toptal if you need one excellent freelance engineer, not a team, and you're prepared to run project management yourself.

Choose N-iX if named large-enterprise clients and third-party analyst recognition (per its Clutch listing) matter more to your vendor-selection process than review volume, and your budget clears $100,000+.

Skip ManasFlow if: you need a headcount of dozens of engineers immediately, which is BairesDev or ELEKS's territory, or you specifically want to manage one freelance hire directly rather than work with a team. We would rather send you to the right fit than force one that doesn't work.

FAQ
What is a product design and development agency?

A product design and development agency handles both the design (user research, UX, interface) and the engineering of a digital product, so one team takes it from wireframe to shipped code. On this list, Netguru is the clearest example of that model, and ManasFlow covers design through build for AI-native products.
What is a software development agency?

A software development agency is a company that designs, builds, and often maintains custom software for clients, as opposed to a platform or marketplace that hands you self-serve tools or an individual freelancer you manage yourself. Agencies typically own a defined scope of work and are accountable for delivery, not just the individual contributor's hours.
How much does it cost to hire a software development agency?

Costs vary by delivery model. Dedicated-team agencies on this list start around $25,000-$50,000 minimum project size with hourly rates of $25-99/hr depending on the firm. Project-based full-service engagements are scoped to the work rather than a flat rate. A marketplace like Toptal charges a monthly subscription plus an hourly rate per engineer, typically $60-150+/hr, with no fixed project minimum since you're hiring one person rather than commissioning a project.
What is the difference between a software development agency and a staffing platform?

An agency owns delivery: it assigns a team, manages the project, and is accountable for the outcome. A staffing platform like Toptal matches you with an individual freelance engineer or a small curated team, but you retain project management, architecture decisions, and quality assurance yourself.
Should I hire a nearshore agency or a local one?

Nearshore agencies (BairesDev, AgileEngine cover Latin America; Netguru and ELEKS cover Eastern Europe) typically offer lower rates than agencies staffed entirely in the US or Western Europe, while keeping working hours reasonably aligned. The tradeoff is less in-person availability. For most software builds, time zone overlap matters more than physical proximity.
How do I evaluate an agency's reviews?

Check the review platform directly (Clutch, G2) rather than testimonials on the agency's own site, since those can be selectively curated. Look at review count, not just star rating: a 5.0/5 rating across 3 reviews carries less statistical weight than a 4.8/5 rating across 86 reviews, even though the star number looks lower. Read a few reviews in full for specifics, not just the aggregate score.
What's the fastest way to get a working product built?

Of the agencies compared here, ManasFlow is the only one that publishes a fixed 30-day delivery window for an MVP as a written commitment rather than a best-effort estimate. Toptal can get you a single engineer working within 5-7 days, but the project timeline from there depends entirely on your own management of that engineer.
Can a software development agency work with my existing tech stack?

Most agencies on this list, ManasFlow included, specialize in integrating with existing systems rather than requiring a rebuild. The real question to ask any agency is whether they have specific, checkable experience with your exact stack (not just "we know everything"), and whether they can show a past integration with a comparable system.
Choosing an agency is a delivery-model decision first, a vendor decision second

The agencies on this list aren't ranked on a single axis because they don't compete on a single axis: a 2,000-person firm and a 20-person AI-native shop solve different problems, even when they answer the same search query. Get the delivery model right first, staff-aug, project-based, or marketplace, then compare the specific agencies inside that category.

ManasFlow is built for the project-based, AI-native end of that spectrum: one senior engineer plus a fleet of agents, a written 30-day MVP commitment, and an embedded-placement option most of the agencies above don't offer.
